//: Development only. HostBaseAddress is where Yello.Host listens under both `dotnet run` and `aspire run`. Story 1.4 moved both projects onto their `https` launch profiles, so this is the https applicationUrl from Yello.Host/Properties/launchSettings.json rather than the http one. There is no appsettings.json sibling: with no configured address the client falls back to its own origin, which is correct for a same-origin deployment. Story 1.10 owns deployment configuration.
//dotnet-run: The `dotnet run` half of that sentence was FALSE until code review on 2026-09-19. Story 1.4 set `launchProfileName: "https"` on the AppHost, which fixed `aspire run` only - `dotnet run` takes the FIRST profile in launchSettings.json, and `http` was still first in both projects. So the Host listened on http://localhost:5026 while this file pointed at https://localhost:7093, every call was a connection refusal shown as a generic submit failure, and CORS failed closed as well because ClientOrigin is injected only by the AppHost. Both launchSettings.json files now put `https` first, which is what makes the sentence above true rather than aspirational.
//nfr-6: NFR-6 says all traffic is encrypted in transit. This was `http://localhost:5026` until story 1.4, and a password crossed the loopback interface in cleartext under `aspire run` - raised at code review on 2026-09-10 and deferred then, because the swap needs `launchProfileName: "https"` on the AppHost plus a trusted dev certificate and could not be verified from a review context. Story 1.4 took it, because AC5 requires the Session cookie to carry `Secure` and a `Secure` cookie is only reliably accepted over https: Chromium treats http://localhost as a secure context, Firefox and Safari do not agree in every version. If a browser warns about the certificate, run `dotnet dev-certs https --trust` once.
//cors: The Host allows exactly the client's own origin, injected by Yello.AppHost from the client resource's https endpoint - so the two sides cannot drift. Nothing about CORS is configured here; this file only says where the Host is.
